results.title: Fast predictive multi-fidelity prediction with models of quantized fidelity levels - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Fast predictive multi-fidelity prediction with models of quantized fidelity levels. Construction of a multi-fidelity predictive model with quantized fidelity levels. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach for the construction of multi-fidelity surrogate models with “discrete” fidelity levels. The notion of a discrete level of fidelity is in contrast to a mathematical model, for which the notion of refinement towards a high-fidelity model is relevant to sending a discretization parameter toward zero in a continuous way. In this study, we propose a multi-fidelity approach for parameterized systems with quantized components that benefits from the efficiency of low-cost models and the accuracy of high-cost models. Thus, in most of these examples the convergence of the low-fidelity model to the high-fidelity model can be proven analytically by refinement of the discretization parameters, and often there is a hierarchical connection between low- and high-fidelity models.

results.title: Full article: Aerodynamic optimization of a coaxial rotor system using a deep learning-based multi-fidelity surrogate model
results.content: This paper introduces a multi-fidelity surrogate-based optimization framework that employs deep learning techniques for aerodynamic optimization of the X2TD coaxial rotor system in hover. To integrate data across three fidelity levels, a Deep Learning-Based Multilevel Hierarchical Kriging (DLMHK) model has been developed, enhancing optimization efficiency by leveraging low– and medium-fidelity simulations. A Multilevel Hierarchical Kriging (MHK) model is built to conduct a deep learning-based multi-fidelity optimization, combining existing low- and medium-fidelity samples with additional high-fidelity data to achieve the optimum. Erhard and Alonso (Citation2024) considered multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization of a coaxial rotor in hover and edgewise flight, based on Blade Element Theory (BET) in conjunction with the Viscous Vortex Particle Method (VVPM). Given the above, this paper proposes a Deep Learning-based Multilevel Hierarchical Kriging (DLMHK) model, aiming to improve the optimization efficiency and enhance the aerodynamic performance of the X2TD coaxial rotor system in hover. In Section 4, a coaxial rotor blade optimization aiming at increasing the figure of merit is conducted using the DLMHK model based on low-, medium- and high-fidelity analysis. The HK model uses two different fidelity of data (e.g. coarse/fine grid or Euler/N-S equation) to improve the optimization efficiency, where the low-fidelity data serve as a trend of global function and the high-fidelity data is employed to enhance the accuracy of data fitting. As shown in Figure , the coaxial rotor optimization is executed by using a deep learning-based multi-fidelity optimization framework, aiming to increase the aerodynamic performance in hover. As depicted in the table, the IGD of MO-DLMHK model is lower than that of MO-Kriging and MO-HK models after 100 iterations, demonstrating that DBN can provide supplementary and reliable low-fidelity samples for multi-objective optimization problem. A multi-fidelity optimization method is employed by using a three-level hierarchical Kriging model to maximize the figure of merit for the coaxial rotor system. In this work, we have developed a deep learning-based multi-fidelity optimization framework, designed to enhance the aerodynamic performance of a coaxial rotor system in hover. The DLMHK-based surrogate model significantly improves the optimization efficiency of a coaxial rotor system, compared to both Kriging and the HK models. An efficient robust aerodynamic design optimization method based on a multi-level hierarchical Kriging model and multi-fidelity expected improvement.

By mapping low-fidelity reduced states to their high-fidelity counterpart, the proposed reduced-order surrogate model enables the efficient recovery of full solution fields over time and parameter variations in a non-intrusive manner.
